anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: A-D survive the course rewrite intact: each keeps P1 open, records the failed prerequisite, avoids a blind retry, and (in D) drafts the surviving-sentence correction without re-applying the confirmed one. E is where After breaks: the record says 'Old-head evidence is discarded', but the fresh-head path then declares 'Evidence re-resolves to CI-sufficient, so there is no local run' and renders 'CI (run 910, ci / test green on 2222222)' - run 910 is the 1111111 check and the digest supplies no check or run for 2222222, so the mergeable verdict and P1 closure rest on old-head evidence relabelled to the new head, exactly what f5 forbids. Before got this right by re-gathering with `gh run list -c 2222...`, finding nothing, falling to the local-run row, running `node --test src/guard.test.ts` at HEAD==2222 with provenance checked, and claim-checking the actual body before resolving P1. To keep f5 under the new course model, make the exact-head evidence rule explicit in the resumed-course text: after a head move, evidence must be re-resolved from checks/runs keyed to the new head, an absent check falls through to a bounded local verification whose head_sha must equal the new head, and the final menu's Evidence line may only cite runs recorded at that head; wording like 're-resolves to CI-sufficient' should be replaced with 'resolve evidence strictly for <new head>; reuse nothing recorded at the pre-move head'. Separately (not a fact here, but worth tightening), A-D's deliver row bundles 'add 6 to each cap' into an ordinary resume after a non-cap obstacle, which conflicts with the Change's intent that extension is offered only when a cap is actually exhausted.

confirmation.feedback: No fact moved: A-C report the 503/502/unexpected-body failures with P1 open and no blind retry, D keeps P1 open after the surviving-contradiction recheck, and E leaves the raced edit unconfirmed and only closes P1 after a fresh Verify/Review and claim check at 2222222. In E, After's Verify helper asserts `source: ci, ci / test green on 2222222` although the digest supplies no check for 2222222; Before handled this by stating the run list for 2222 was empty and resolving to the local-run fallback. Keep that pattern: show the `gh run list -c 2222...` read, state that no check exists for the new head, and bind readiness to the local verification log (or an explicit pending-CI initial menu) rather than letting a helper assert CI evidence that was never read, otherwise a careful reader can call the closure an unsupported clean assertion.
